title: Independence, exclusion, and inclusion-exclusion
terms: independent events; mutually independent events; pairwise independence; mutually exclusive events; inclusion-exclusion; conditional probability; Bayes theorem; law of total probability.

exposition.text:
Events A, B are independent when P (A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B). Mutually exclusive events have
empty intersection; positive-probability mutually exclusive events are not independent. Always
P(A ∪ B) = P (A) + P (B) − P(A ∩ B). Events are mutually independent when every finite

question.text:
Events A, B are independent with P(A) = 2/5 and P(B) = 3/4. What is P (A | A ∪ B)?
(A) 4/17 (B) 6/17 (C) 8/17 (D) 1/2 (E) 3/5

solution.text:
The union has probability 2/5 + 3/4 − (2/5)(3/4) = 17/20. Since A ∩ (A ∪ B) = A, the
conditional probability is (2/5)/(17/20) = 8/17.

question.text:
Events A, B, C are pairwise independent, each of probability 1/2, and P (A ∩ B ∩ C) = 0. What
is P (A ∪ B ∪ C)?
(A) 1/2 (B) 5/8 (C) 3/4 (D) 7/8 (E) 1

solution.text:
Pairwise independence gives each pairwise intersection probability 1/4. Inclusion-exclusion
gives 3(1/2) − 3(1/4) + 0 = 3/4. The triple intersection cannot be replaced by 1/8 because
mutual independence was not assumed.

question.text:
Events A, B are independent and satisfy A ∩ B = ∅. Which conclusion must hold?
(A) A = ∅
(B) B = ∅
(C) At least one of A, B is empty.
(D) P(A) = 0 or P(B) = 0
(E) P(A) + P (B) = 1

solution.text:
Independence gives P(A)P (B) = P (A ∩ B) = 0. Since probabilities are nonnegative, at
least one is zero. That event need not be empty: two distinct singleton events in a uni-
form continuous sample space are disjoint, nonempty, and independent because both have
probability zero.

question.text:
Only P(A) = 3/5 and P(B) = 3/4 are known. What is the full possible range of P (A | B)?
(A) [0, 1] (B) [7/15, 4/5] (C) [3/5, 3/4] (D) [1/5, 4/5] (E) [7/20, 3/5]

solution.text:
The intersection satisfies max(0, P (A) + P (B) − 1) ≤ P (A ∩ B) ≤ min(P (A), P(B)), giving
7/20 ≤ P (A ∩ B) ≤ 3/5. Dividing by 3/4 gives [7/15, 4/5]. Every intermediate intersection is
attainable by assigning nonnegative probabilities to the four membership regions, so this is
the full range.
